parts.article:
Science and Filmmaking
 
Academics are now working more with filmmakers who are impressed by the results of their research in computer-generated imagery (CGI)
 
(A) Every year the film academy in the USA celebrates the outstanding achievements of the year in a ceremony known as the Oscars. An increasingly important component of the ceremony is the presentation of the Scientific and Technical awards. In 2004 a notable event took place: the academic world met the cinematographic world when researchers from Stanford University in the USA were awarded an Oscar. These researchers, led by Steve Marschner, were from the field of Computer Graphics at Stanford. They were part of a growing cohort of computer scientists that has become fundamental to moviemaking.
 
(B) Films have shown that it is possible to use CGI to make actors look younger, older, weaker or stronger than they actually are in a surprisingly realistic manner. At least, it is possible if the altered actors are not filmed too closely. This is because the difficulty of recreating the textures of both skin and fabric means that the effect is less convincing when seen close up. The work of Marschner and his colleagues has greatly improved the accurate and realistic modeling of both skin and fabric. They recognized that one of the difficulties of creating lifelike characters in the computer world is that, in CGI, the characters’ skin is opaque (two-dimensional) whereas real skin is in fact translucent (three-dimensional), that is to say, it is semi-transparent.
 
(C) Marschner and his colleagues received the Oscar for their work in successfully producing a CGI model that simulates translucency; this is when light penetrates skin and then scatters below the skin’s surface before re-emerging. This is called subsurface scattering, and the mathematics for the model goes back many decades to the time when it was used in astrophysics. Because human skin is naturally translucent, it was necessary to be able to create this artificially in order to simulate the soft appearance of real skin. Previous CGI models, which assumed that skin was entirely opaque, resulted in characters with a plastic appearance. The scientists’ new model of CGI was so important in bringing digital characters to life that, within two years of their original research paper, all the major special-effects studios had incorporated it into their digital rendering systems.
 
(D) However, despite their award, the scientists, with admirable tenacity, continued their search for perfection, as they still did not feel that they had yet satisfactorily recreated the subtle ways light is reflected. To do this, they began to look in detail at the way skins and fabrics reflect light differently according to their make-up: the exact arrangement of fibers in fabric and the network of fibers in skin. Marschner and his team tried to do this by using computerized tomography, which is most familiar as a medical technique for examining people’s internal organs. Like classical radiology, it uses X-rays, but because the image is constructed inside a computer using exposures taken from many different positions, rather than a single exposure on photographic film, it can capture fine details that are invisible in classical radiography.
 
(E) Unfortunately, the scientists understood that at this point in time they could not use computerized tomography on skin, because a very high-intensity X-ray is needed to show the kind of detail they wanted and this would be very dangerous for human skin. They have, however, had some success with fabric. Using this new method of imaging, they are able to accurately record the three-dimensional structure of all the fibers in a number of small pieces of fabric. These same pieces of fabric, through the use of CGI, can then be patched together to form an entire garment inside a computer, in the same way that a small group of actors can be made to look like hundreds of people gathered together. A garment created through CGI is therefore made up of pieces of fabric whose internal structure has been pre-recorded. This means that the way light is reflected by the garment can be calculated far more realistically than if the scientists just made a computer model of what they thought the interior of the fabric looked like. Cinematography will benefit from this because, although it may take some years to be able to use computerized tomographic imaging of skin, for the moment the movement of a virtual cloak or the lifting of a computerized hat should look far more realistic.
 
(F) In the meantime, according to Marschner’s colleague Kavita Bala, the technology might have an application in online retailing. At the moment, people buying clothes over the internet have only a standard photograph to help them choose their purchases. It is hoped that if online shoppers can view items which have been presented through the use of computerized tomography graphics, they will have a much better understanding of what the material the item is made of is really like. Marschner is now working on the way light is scattered from individual hairs. He says, ‘I feel lucky to be working in this niche. I’m a visual person and to be able to spend my time scrutinizing the world around me, trying to understand why it looks the way it does, is very rewarding’.
parts.questions:
Questions 27–32
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 27–32 on your answer sheet.

Q27 What is the writer’s main point in the first paragraph?

  • A Computer scientists are rarely represented at the Oscars.
  • B Film-industry awards hold little interest for computer scientists.
  • C The USA rewards film actors more than computer scientists.
  • D Computer scientists are becoming a vital part of the film industry.

Q28 When describing the way computer-generated imagery changes actors’ appearance, what does the writer suggest?

  • A CGI looks best from a distance.
  • B CGI interferes with actors’ facial expressions.
  • C Audiences expect too much of CGI.
  • D The scientists had hoped for more convincing results.

Q29 What does the writer suggest about the scientists’ attitude to their work in the fourth paragraph?

  • A They were motivated to get as near to reality as possible.
  • B They were interested in gaining recognition for their work.
  • C They thought it could have medical applications.
  • D They hoped to receive further funding for their research.

Q30 What are we told about computerised tomography?

  • A It has only recently been used by doctors.
  • B It is similar to X-rays in the way it works.
  • C Filmmakers have used it for many years for special lighting effects.
  • D It can be administered using traditional radiography machines.

Q31 Which of these advantages does the writer attribute to the current use of computerised tomography?

  • A It is most effective when used to create images of skin.
  • B It can make a few people seem like a crowd.
  • C It allows clothes designers to create new designs.
  • D It is practical because of the time it takes.

Q32 The writer mentions Kavita Bala in order to

  • A comment on the success of CGI in commercial contexts.
  • B highlight the link between CGI and photography.
  • C show that Marschner’s team are uncertain about the future of CGI.
  • D demonstrate a use for CGI outside the film industry.
Questions 33–36
Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 3?
In boxes 33–36 on your answer sheet, write:

Q33 It used to be unusual for university researchers to receive a cinematography award.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q34 CGI is popular among ageing actors.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q35 The scientists’ success in generating images of complete CGI garments has won them many awards.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q36 It will be a long time before computerised tomographic imaging of fabric is used by filmmakers.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN
Questions 37–40
Complete the summary using the list of words, A-I, below.
Write the correct letter, A-I, in boxes 37–40 on your answer sheet.
The work of Marschner and his colleagues
For many years, CGI characters did not appear entirely lifelike as their skin appeared plastic. Marschner and his colleagues were the first to apply an understanding of how interacts with human skin. Their CGI model is based on a novel application of principles of , which had previously been applied in other scientific research. The importance of CGI to the film industry has led to the of Marschner’s model by special-effects studios. Marschner’s model has led to the of cinematography.
  • A light
  • B transparency
  • C age
  • D use
  • E astrophysics
  • F mathematics
  • G improvement
  • H colour
  • I translucency

reference:
Q27

干扰 “Fundamental” 意为不可或缺，对应选项中的 “vital part”。A（奥斯卡很少有）、B（没兴趣）、C（美国更奖励演员）均与文意（notable event, awarded, fundamental）不符。

句子 (Paragraph A) "They were part of a growing cohort of computer scientists that has become fundamental to moviemaking."

解析 题目问第一段作者的中心观点是什么。第一段提到学术界与电影界的相遇（academics met cinematographic world），并指出计算机科学家群体已成为电影制作的“fundamental（基础/至关重要）”部分，对应选项 D（计算机科学家正成为电影业的重要组成部分）。

Q28

解析 题目问描述CGI改变演员外貌时作者暗示了什么。B段提到如果被修改的演员“not filmed too closely（不拍太近）”是可行的，因为近看“less convincing（不那么令人信服）”，暗示远看效果最好，对应选项 A。

干扰 “Looks best from a distance” 是对原文 “less convincing when seen close up” 的反向逻辑推导。

句子 (Paragraph B) "At least, it is possible if the altered actors are not filmed too closely... less convincing when seen close up."

Q29

解析 题目问第四段暗示科学家对工作的态度是什么。D段提到尽管获奖，他们仍“continued their search for perfection（继续追求完美）”，因为觉得尚未“satisfactorily recreated（满意地重现）”光反射的微妙方式，即力求逼真，对应选项 A（有动力尽可能接近现实）。

干扰 “Get as near to reality as possible” 对应原文的 “search for perfection / satisfactorily recreated”。

句子 (Paragraph D) "...continued their search for perfection, as they still did not feel that they had yet satisfactorily recreated..."

Q30

句子 (Paragraph D) "Like classical radiology, it uses X-rays, but because the image is constructed inside a computer..."

解析 题目问关于CT扫描（computerised tomography）我们得知了什么。D段提到它“Like classical radiology, it uses X-rays（像传统放射学一样，它使用X射线）”，对应选项 B（在工作方式上与X光相似）。

干扰 题目问的是关于CT的事实，原文直接用 “Like... uses X-rays” 进行了类比。

Q31

解析 题目问作者将哪个优势归因于目前CT的使用。E段提到利用CT扫描织物的小块，可以像“small group of actors can be made to look like hundreds（把一小群演员做得看起来像几百人）”那样拼接成整件衣服，对应选项 B。

干扰 这是一个类比选项，作者用“以少变多（make a few seem like a crowd）”来形容CT技术在织物建模上的高效复用优势。

句子 (Paragraph E) "...can then be patched together... in the same way that a small group of actors can be made to look like hundreds of people gathered together."

Q32

解析 题目问提到Kavita Bala是为了什么。F段提到该技术可能在“online retailing（在线零售）”有应用，这属于电影行业之外的领域，对应选项 D。

干扰 “Outside the film industry” 对应 “online retailing”。

句子 (Paragraph F) "...the technology might have an application in online retailing."

Q33

解析 题目说大学研究人员获得电影类奖项曾是不常见的。A段提到2004年发生了一件“notable event（值得注意的/不寻常的事件）”：学术界与电影界相遇并获奖，暗示此前罕见，选 YES。

干扰 “Unusual” 对应原文的 “notable event” 和 “academic world met...”。

句子 (Paragraph A) "In 2004 a notable event took place: the academic world met the cinematographic world..."

Q34

干扰 文中只说了技术能做什么（Look younger/older），没说演员对此的主观态度。

句子 (Paragraph B) "Films have shown that it is possible to use CGI to make actors look younger, older..."

解析 题目说CGI在年长演员中很受欢迎。B段只提到CGI能让演员看起来更年轻或更老，未提及演员本人是否“popular（喜欢/欢迎）”这项技术，选 NOT GIVEN。

Q35

解析 题目说科学家在生成完整CGI服装图像方面的成功为他们赢得了许多奖项。文殊提到他们因“皮肤半透明（translucency）”研究获奥斯卡，后文提到在服装（garment）上的成功是获奖之后的事，并未提及服装研究是否“won many awards”，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 获奖的是皮肤模型，服装研究是在获奖后进行的（continued their search），不要张冠李戴。

句子 (Paragraph C/D/E) 获奖针对 skin translucency; Garment success 发生在 Paragraph E，未提奖项。

Q36

解析 题目说电影制作人使用织物的CT成像还需要很长时间。E段末尾对比说：尽管皮肤CT可能需要几年，但“for the moment（目前/现在）”虚拟斗篷（织物）的运动看起来应该更真实了，即织物技术现在已可用，选 NO。

干扰 题目说“fabric... long time”，原文说“skin... some years”但“cloak (fabric)... for the moment”，对象搞反了。

句子 (Paragraph E) "...although it may take some years to be able to use... imaging of skin, for the moment the movement of a virtual cloak..."

Q37

句子 (Paragraph C) "...this is when light penetrates skin and then scatters..."

解析 题目说Marschner等人首先应用了关于____如何与人类皮肤相互作用的理解。C段提到这是当“light penetrates skin（光穿透皮肤）”时发生的，填 light。

干扰 “Interacts with” 对应原文的 “penetrates... and then scatters”。

Q38

解析 题目说他们的CGI模型基于____原理的新应用，这些原理以前曾用于其他科学研究。C段提到该模型的“mathematics（数学）”可以追溯到几十年前在天体物理学中的使用，填 mathematics。

干扰 题目是“principles of ______”，原文是“the mathematics for the model”，astrophysics是应用领域而非原理本身。

句子 (Paragraph C) "...the mathematics for the model goes back many decades to the time when it was used in astrophysics."

Q39

解析 题目说CGI对电影业的重要性导致特效工作室对Marschner模型的____。C段末尾提到工作室已将其“incorporated（合并/采用）”进系统，对应选项 use（使用/采用）。

干扰 “Incorporated” 在这里即“adoption”或“use”的同义替换。

句子 (Paragraph C) "...all the major special-effects studios had incorporated it into their digital rendering systems."

Q40

解析 题目说Marschner的模型导致了电影摄影的____。E段末尾说电影摄影将“benefit from（受益于）”这一点，看起来更真实，即带来了改进，对应选项 improvement。

干扰 “Led to the ______” 对应原文的 “will benefit from this / look far more realistic”。

句子 (Paragraph E) "Cinematography will benefit from this because... should look far more realistic."
